summary: A progressive brain disorder that gradually destroys memory and thinking skills and eventually interferes with the ability to carry out everyday activities
common_symptoms: Memory loss; confusion; impaired reasoning or judgment; word-finding difficulty; visual-spatial difficulties; difficulty completing everyday tasks; mood or personality changes
source_summary: National Institute on Aging (NIH); FDA; verified 2026-09-08

summary: A progressive neurological disorder in which nerve cells involved in movement become impaired or die, leading to reduced dopamine signaling and progressively impaired movement
common_symptoms: Tremor; muscle rigidity; bradykinesia; impaired balance and coordination; gait difficulties; speech difficulties; sleep problems; constipation; depression; cognitive changes; fatigue; reduced sense of smell
source_summary: NIH National Institute on Aging; National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke; verified 2026-09-08

summary: A progressive neurodegenerative disease that affects motor neurons in the brain and spinal cord, leading to progressive loss of voluntary muscle control
common_symptoms: Muscle weakness; muscle twitching (fasciculations); muscle cramps; muscle stiffness or spasticity; muscle atrophy; slurred speech; difficulty chewing or swallowing; difficulty walking; progressive breathing difficulties
source_summary: NIH National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS); verified 2026-09-08

summary: A chronic autoimmune neurological disorder in which the immune system damages structures of the central nervous system, disrupting communication between the brain, spinal cord, and other parts of the body
common_symptoms: Vision problems; numbness or tingling; muscle weakness; muscle stiffness or spasms; fatigue; balance and coordination problems; walking difficulties; bladder or bowel problems; pain; cognitive changes
source_summary: NIH National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS); verified 2026-09-08

summary: A chronic neurological disorder characterized by recurrent seizures resulting from abnormal electrical activity in the brain
common_symptoms: Involuntary movements or jerking; muscle stiffening; staring or lapses in awareness; altered sensations; unusual behaviors; loss of awareness or consciousness; confusion or fatigue after a seizure
source_summary: NIH National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS); verified 2026-09-08

summary: A neurological disorder characterized by recurrent headache attacks that may occur with or without aura and are often accompanied by other neurological and systemic symptoms
common_symptoms: Moderate-to-severe headache; throbbing or pulsating pain; nausea or vomiting; sensitivity to light; sensitivity to sound; fatigue; visual disturbances or other aura symptoms; numbness or tingling; difficulty speaking
source_summary: NIH National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS); verified 2026-09-08

summary: A chronic neuromuscular disease that causes weakness of the voluntary muscles, including muscles involved in eye and eyelid movement, facial expression, swallowing, speech, limb movement, and breathing
common_symptoms: Muscle weakness that may worsen with activity; drooping eyelids; double or blurred vision; facial weakness; difficulty speaking; difficulty chewing or swallowing; weakness of the arms, hands, legs, or neck; shortness of breath
source_summary: NIH National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS); verified 2026-09-08

summary: An inherited, progressive neurological disorder that causes neurons in parts of the brain to gradually break down and die, affecting movement, cognition, behavior, and emotion
common_symptoms: Chorea or involuntary movements; abnormal postures; impaired coordination and balance; difficulty walking; problems with thinking, judgment, memory, planning, or organization; behavioral or personality changes; emotional or psychiatric symptoms
source_summary: NIH National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS); verified 2026-09-08

summary: An inherited neuromuscular disease in which loss of functional SMN1 leads to degeneration of lower motor neurons, causing progressive muscle weakness and muscle wasting
common_symptoms: Muscle weakness; reduced muscle tone; diminished or absent reflexes; muscle twitching or fasciculations; difficulty sitting, standing, or walking; difficulty swallowing or feeding; breathing difficulties; scoliosis or other skeletal abnormalities
source_summary: NIH National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS); verified 2026-09-08
